theater: 多瑙河下游與達契亞山區

battle.name: 第一次達契亞戰爭
battle.theater: 多瑙河下游與達契亞山區
battle.brief: 前101年圖拉真領羅馬大軍越過多瑙河，在圖帕埃打開缺口，翌年奪取達契亞王都薩爾米澤蓋圖薩，逼得德塞巴魯斯自盡。卡面那把羅馬短劍是軍團步兵的標準配劍：在鐵門峽谷架橋、攀攻山堡與雪季扎營的苦撐裡，它是最後幾步才出手的兵器，真正吃掉戰役的是工兵、弓手和攻城槓。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 第一次達契亞戰爭（公元101年—102年）是羅馬帝國與達契亞王國之間的一場邊境戰爭，戰場在今日羅馬尼亞境內的多瑙河下游與喀爾巴阡山之間。羅馬一方由皇帝圖拉真親自統率，他既是最高指揮官，也是整場戰爭的策劃者：兵種包括近衛的十餘個帝國軍團（第二團、第五「馬其頓」團、第十三「雙子」團是帝國邊防的骨幹），由各行省抽調的輔助步兵與騎兵，來自敘利亞與安納托利亞的弓手，以及高盧與不列顛調來的投射兵與軍馬；指揮系統由多瑙河下游兩個行省的總督府調度，後方靠地中海航線把糧秣、攻城器械與補充兵員從奧斯蒂亞與拉文納運往戰區。達契亞一方是卡爾巴阡山各支達契亞與蓋特氏族拼成的王國，國王德塞巴魯斯同時握有最高軍事權與祭祀權，王國另有戴羊毛帽的「塔拉鮑斯特」祭司階層掌宗教與立法；軍隊是臨時徵召的部落戰團，步兵以長矛、彎刀與巨大的橢圓盾為主，另有弓手與重騎兵，沒有常備兵員，也沒有能連續供應的攻城器械。戰前兩軍隔多瑙河對峙：羅馬在北岸設有多瑙河堡壘群，達契亞的堡壘則沿山脈呈網狀分布，構成一道難攻的防守骨架。
countriesEn: The First Dacian War (AD 101–102) was a frontier war between the Roman Empire and the Dacian Kingdom, fought in what is now Romania, between the lower Danube and the Carpathian mountains. Rome's side was commanded personally by the emperor Trajan, who was both supreme commander and the planner of the whole campaign. His troops included a dozen or more imperial legions on the frontier list (the Second, the Fifth Macedonica and the Thirteenth Gemina were the backbone of the imperial border), auxiliary infantry and cavalry drawn from the provinces, archers from Syria and Anatolia, and slingers and horses contributed by Gaul and Britain. Command was arranged through the governorships of the two Danubian provinces below, and behind them the Mediterranean sea lanes carried grain, siege equipment and replacements from Ostia and Ravenna to the theatre. The Dacian side was a kingdom assembled from Dacian and Getic clans of the Carpathians, in which King Decebalus held the highest military and priestly authority, while a class of 'tarabostes' priests, marked by the woollen cap they wore, controlled religion and law. Their army was a levy of tribal war-bands: infantry armed with long spears, curved swords and huge oval shields, supported by archers and heavy cavalry, with no standing army and no siege train that could be supplied continuously. Before the war the two armies faced each other across the Danube. Rome held a chain of forts on the northern bank, while the Dacian forts were distributed in a network along the mountains, forming a defensive skeleton that was hard to break.
people: 這場戰爭的最高人物是普布利烏斯·埃爾維利烏斯·圖拉真（Marcus Ulpius Traianus，公元98年至117年在位）。他在前100年出任下多瑙河總督，戰前一年以皇帝身分駐節伊利里亞，在總督府所在的城市整備軍需、徵召船隻、囤積糧食，然後把越河作戰當成自己的事業，而不是交給邊軍處理。圖拉真左右有兩類人：一類是工程師，阿波羅多托斯（Apollodorus of Damascus）在公元100年後奉召入軍，主持了鐵門峽谷的棧道與浮橋，後來又主持圖拉真廣場與圖拉真柱的設計；另一類是軍團級指揮官，哈德良當時以待護軍（legatus legionis）的身分在軍中服務，據史家記載，他出現在與達契亞人議和的使者行列裡。達契亞方面的關鍵人物是國王德塞巴魯斯（Decebalus）：公元85年達契亞人越河擊殺下多瑙河總督穆奇亞努斯之後他迅速崛起，在公元87年至88年的圖帕埃戰役中先勝後敗，弟弟死在第二次交鋒裡，卻也靠著迫使圖密善放棄追究的實力，在割地與納貢的條件下維持了十餘年的和平。公元101年他再撕毀默契，最後選擇死亡而不是投降。卡西烏斯·迪奧尼烏斯（Cassius Dio）是唯一留下成篇同期敘述的人，他身為元老院議員，寫下了渡河、山地追擊與國王自盡的經過；後世喬達內斯（ Jordanes）的達契亞傳說則為這場戰爭補上另一層戲劇化的外衣。
peopleEn: The central figure was Publius Aelius Traianus (Marcus Ulpius Traianus, emperor from AD 98 to 117). He had been governor of Lower Moesia in AD 100, and in the year before the war he took up residence in Illyricum as emperor, at the seat of the provincial governor, where he gathered grain, requisitioned shipping and stockpiled supplies, and then treated the crossing of the river as his own enterprise rather than a task to be handed to the frontier army. Two kinds of men stood around him. One was the engineer: Apollodorus of Damascus was called into the army after AD 100, and directed the road and the pontoon bridge through the Iron Gates, and later designed the Forum of Trajan and Trajan's Column. The other was the legionary commander: Hadrian was then serving in the army with the rank of legatus legionis, and the sources list him among the envoys who negotiated with the Dacians. The key figure on the Dacian side was King Decebalus. After the Dacians crossed the river in AD 85 and killed the governor of Lower Moesia, Mucianus, he rose quickly; in the fighting at Tapae in AD 87 and 88 he won once and then lost, and his brother was killed in the second engagement, yet the strength that forced Domitian to drop the matter also bought him more than a decade of peace on conditions of ceded land and tribute. In AD 101 he tore that agreement up again, and at the end he chose death rather than surrender. Cassius Dio is the only man to leave a continuous contemporary narrative; a senator himself, he wrote out the crossing, the pursuit through the mountains and the king's suicide. Jordanes' later Getic history added a second, more dramatic layer to the same story.
kits: 卡面是羅馬短劍（gladius）：直刃、雙刃、尖端略收，刃長約六十公分，連柄不過七十公分出頭，是帝國軍團步兵的標準佩劍。它的功能從來不是揮砍，短兵相接時士兵用盾牌的邊緣卡住對方的武器，再以短促的刺擊收拾距離。所以在這場戰役裡，短劍真正的位置在最末端：渡河與築路靠工兵，山地行軍靠糧秣與秩序，攻破圖帕埃堡壘靠弓手與攻城槓，投石機與弩砲才是啃骨頭的部分。羅馬步兵的完整配置是橢圓形大盾（scutum）加重標槍（pilum），以「投矛洗臉、彎刀收割」的次序展開；護甲有分段式板甲（lorica segmentata）與鎖子甲（lorica hamata）兩種，頭盔是帝國式鐵盔（galea）；營地按每日行程搭建，木柵、壕溝、帳幕、畜欄一應俱全，帳篷由牛皮張成，牛拉著載滿穀物與柴薪的車。輔助兵與騎兵的配備不同：騎兵用較長的雙手劍（spatha）與長矛，色雷斯與巴塔維亞騎兵各按自己的傳統作戰，弓手用弓，或用標槍與石彈。達契亞方面的裝備同樣有明顯標誌：步兵裝備外彎的鐮刀劍（falx），羅馬尼亞康斯坦察出土的這類鐵劍弧度大、刃厚，專為在窄地帶劈砍而設計，這正是羅馬工兵最怕遇到的局面；配合鳥形面甲的青銅與鐵盔（考古上稱「德塞巴魯斯型」）、箭袋（gorytos）、橢圓大盾與長矛。堡壘以石牆、削尖木柵與梯道構成，羅馬軍則帶著圍城用的帳棚（vinea）、柴束、攻城塔與弩砲上門。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman gladius: a straight, double-edged blade with a slightly tapered point, about sixty centimetres of blade and no more than seventy centimetres overall including the hilt, the standard sidearm of the imperial legionary infantryman. Its function was never to slash: in close combat the soldier used the rim of his shield to catch the enemy's weapon and finished the business with a short thrust, so the sword's real place in this campaign was at the very end of the chain. Crossing the river and cutting the road belonged to the engineers, marching through the mountains belonged to the commissariat and to discipline, breaking the fort at Tapae belonged to the archers and the artillery, and the ballistae and stone-throwers were the instruments that actually did the biting. The complete Roman infantry loadout was the oval scutum with the heavy pilum, fought in the sequence of flurrying the face with javelins and then harvesting with the sword; armour came as segmented plate (lorica segmentata) or chain mail (lorica hamata), the head was covered by the imperial iron galea, and the camp was pitched to the day's march with palisade, ditch, tents and cattle lines, the tents of stretched ox-hide and the wagons drawn by oxen and loaded with grain and firewood. Auxiliaries and cavalry were equipped differently: the horsemen carried the longer two-handed spatha and long spears, Thracian and Batavian riders fought in their own traditions, and the archers used the bow or the javelin with stone shot. The Dacian equipment is just as distinctive: their infantry carried the out-curving falx, and the iron swords of this type excavated at Constanța in Romania have a strong curve and a thick edge, made for chopping in confined ground, which was precisely the situation Roman engineers most feared to meet. They went with bronze and iron helmets with bird-of-prey face masks, which archaeology calls the 'Decebalus type', the gorytos quiver, the great oval shield and long spears. The forts were built of stone walls, sharpened stakes and stepped approaches, while the Roman column brought up the vinea, bundles of brushwood, siege towers and ballistae for the siege.
tactics: 把狄奧的敘述與考古證據合起來看，這場戰爭的戰術可以分作四段。第一段是渡河與突破：圖拉真不在寬闊的河段強渡，而選在最狹窄的鐵門峽谷一帶動工，先在峭壁間開鑿棧道，再用舟船搭成浮橋，把大軍連同輜重一次過送過多瑙河；這條路後來成為羅馬人進入達契亞山區的固定通道。渡河之後羅馬不讓達契亞人挑戰場地，而是主動進攻，先掃掉北岸與東側的達契亞堡壘，其中圖帕埃是關鍵，攻下它等於打開通往摩爾多瓦河上游的門戶。第二段是山地追擊：達契亞軍隊退入堡壘群後，羅馬的做法不是硬攻，而是以工兵在岩壁中掘進坑道（cuniculi），試圖從守軍以為安全的岩體內部直抵核心；薩爾米澤蓋圖薩一帶出土的羅馬掘進坑道長達一千五百米上下，正是這套辦法的痕跡。第三段是攻城：堡壘外牆高、通道狹窄、入口常只有一條，羅馬人先用重標槍與弩砲壓制牆頭守軍，用柴束與帳棚搭出移動掩體，再以密集隊形護送攻城器械逼近，最後才由短劍手清理狹窄通道裡的守軍。第四段是撤退：冬季來臨、山路被雪封住、糧秣告急，圖拉真沒有強行追到底，而是在奪下王都與國庫之後主動收兵。整體看，這是一場以工程、投射火力與後勤取勝的戰爭，達契亞的山地堡壘體系幾乎把短劍的作用壓到最小。
tacticsEn: If Dio's narrative is set against the archaeological evidence, the tactics of this war fall into four phases. The first was the crossing and the breakthrough. Trajan did not force the river on a broad front; he chose the narrowest reach, at the Iron Gates gorge, put the engineers to work there, cut a road and shelf along the cliff, and then lashed boats into a pontoon bridge so that the army and its baggage passed over the Danube in one movement; that road afterwards became the fixed approach by which Roman troops entered the Dacian mountains. Once across, Rome did not allow the Dacians to choose the ground; it attacked, clearing the Dacian forts on the northern bank and to the east, and the key among them was Tapae, whose fall opened the way up towards the upper Moldavia. The second phase was the pursuit in the mountains. When the Dacian army withdrew into its network of forts, Rome did not simply assault the walls: engineers drove mining galleries (cuniculi) through the rock, trying to reach the core from inside the mass the defenders considered safe. The Roman galleries excavated at Sarmizegetusa run to roughly fifteen hundred metres, and they are the physical trace of exactly that method. The third phase was the siege. The fort walls were high, the approaches narrow, the entrance often a single gate, so the Romans first used heavy javelins and ballistae to silence the defenders on the wall, then built moving shelters out of brushwood and hide (vineae), escorted the siege engines forward in close order, and only at the last stage did the swordsmen clear the defenders out of the narrow passages. The fourth phase was the withdrawal: winter came, the mountain roads were closed by snow, supplies ran short, and Trajan did not force the pursuit to the bitter end but broke off after taking the royal capital and its treasure, leaving the rest of the war to a later expedition. Taken as a whole, this was a war won by engineering, missile fire and logistics, and the Dacian system of mountain fortresses reduced the gladius to its smallest possible role.
data: 這場戰爭留下可核對的數字不多，能確定的部分可分成軍力、行程、遺址與戰利品四塊。軍力方面，現代研究一般認為圖拉真第一次出兵時投入的帝國軍主力在數萬人量級，軍團約十個上下，加上輔助步兵、弓手、騎兵與工兵；到第二次戰役，駐紮達契亞的帝國軍團增加到十三個以上，輔助兵團與騎兵的總數沒有留下可靠記錄。達契亞王國的疆域估計在十萬平方公里上下，人口常被估為五十萬至一百萬，兩者都是分歧很大的推算，不宜當作精確值。行程方面，多瑙河鐵門渡口到奧爾什蒂耶山區王都的直線距離約一百三十公里；北部的圖帕埃到王都直線接近三百六十公里，山路繞行自然更長。遺址方面，奧爾什蒂耶山區被確認的達契亞堡壘有數十座，核心是王都所在的薩爾米澤蓋圖薩與周邊數座同級堡壘；羅馬人在王都留下的掘進坑道總長約一千五百米，營壘、壕溝與柱洞由一九二四至一九二八年帕爾萬主持的發掘所確認。紀念物方面，圖拉真柱高約三十八米，螺旋浮雕帶長約一百三十七米，刻出的人物多達五千以上，公元113年落成。戰利品方面，後世著作常引用「黃金約十六萬五千磅、銀約三十一萬磅」這樣的估算，數字來自獲利一方的記載，應視為上限而非實數。至於雙方傷亡，史料幾乎沒有留下可信數字，能確定的只是羅馬在第一次戰役中損失輕微，而達契亞方面在圖帕埃的營帳被奪、許多人被俘。
dataEn: Few checkable numbers survive from this war, and what can be fixed falls into four blocks. On strength, modern studies generally put the imperial element Trajan took across the Danube in 101 at a force of tens of thousands, with something like ten legions, to which were added auxiliary infantry, archers, cavalry and engineers; by the second war the number of imperial legions garrisoned in Dacia had risen to more than thirteen, and no reliable tally of the auxiliary cohorts and cavalry survives. The Dacian kingdom is estimated at something on the order of a hundred thousand square kilometres of territory and a population commonly put between five hundred thousand and a million, both of them contested estimates that should not be treated as exact. On distance, the straight line from the Danube crossing at the Iron Gates to the royal capital in the Orăștie mountains is about a hundred and thirty kilometres, while the straight line from Tapae in the north to the capital is close to three hundred and sixty kilometres, and the mountain road was of course longer still. On archaeology, a few dozen Dacian forts have been identified in the Orăștie valley, the core of them being Sarmizegetusa Regia and several other forts of the same rank; the Roman mining galleries left at the capital run to about fifteen hundred metres in total, and the camp, ditch and post-holes were confirmed by the excavations Vasile Pârvan directed between 1924 and 1928. On monuments, Trajan's Column stands about thirty-eight metres high, its spiral relief band about a hundred and thirty-seven metres long, with upwards of five thousand figures carved on it, and it was dedicated in AD 113. On booty, later works quote an estimate of roughly a hundred and sixty-five thousand pounds of gold and three hundred and ten thousand pounds of silver; the figure comes from the account of the victors and should be read as a ceiling rather than a true sum. On casualties the record is almost silent, and the only thing that can be fixed is that Roman losses in the first campaign were light, while on the Dacian side the camp at Tapae was taken and many men were captured.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分成遠因、近因與導火線三層。遠因是羅馬在多瑙河下游的邊境政策：公元85年達契亞人越河擊殺下多瑙河總督穆奇亞努斯並劫掠行省，圖密善雖然派軍討伐，卻在公元88年圖帕埃的第二次交鋒中被達契亞人擊退，最後只能讓德塞巴魯斯成為帶著附庸條件的國王，這等於羅馬默認多瑙河不是可靠的國界，達契亞王國也從此獲得向外擴張的空間。近因是圖拉真即位後的整套政策：他不滿於維持現狀，要恢復此前羅馬在多瑙河以北的影響，並把防線推到喀爾巴阡山內側；他調兵、徵船、修路，把這場戰爭當作自己的帝國事業來經營。導火線在公元101年爆發，德塞巴魯斯在鐵門一帶堵塞羅馬堡壘，又殺死送信的羅馬騎士，談判破裂；羅馬要求歸還掠奪物並維持原有條約，德塞巴魯斯不接受，圖拉真於是取得元老院的支持出兵。值得說明的是，開戰前德塞巴魯斯也做過外交：據狄奧記載，他先派使節求和並願意交出人質，但羅馬開出的代價超出他願意付出的程度，於是雙方都把對方的條件視為羞辱。兩個部族國家之間那條勉強維持了十餘年的線，就這樣斷了。
causeEn: The reasons for fighting fall into three layers: a distant cause, a proximate cause and a trigger. The distant cause was Roman frontier policy on the lower Danube. In AD 85 the Dacians crossed the river, killed the governor of Lower Moesia, Mucianus, and plundered the province; Domitian sent an army to punish them, but after the second engagement at Tapae in AD 88 the Romans were beaten back and had to settle for making Decebalus a king under client conditions. That amounted to a Roman admission that the Danube was not a reliable frontier, and it gave the Dacian kingdom room to expand. The proximate cause was the whole policy of Trajan after his accession: unwilling to leave things as they were, he meant to recover the Roman position north of the Danube and push the line of defence inside the Carpathians, and he moved troops, requisitioned shipping and built roads, treating the war as an imperial enterprise of his own. The trigger came in AD 101, when Decebalus blockaded the Roman fort at the Iron Gates and killed a Roman horseman carrying a message, and the talks broke down. Rome demanded the return of the plunder and the maintenance of the existing treaty; Decebalus would not accept it, and Trajan obtained the senate's backing for war. It is worth noting that Decebalus also tried diplomacy before the fighting: Dio records that he sent envoys to seek peace and offered hostages, but the price Rome asked exceeded what he was willing to pay, and each side read the other's terms as an insult. The line that had held between two tribal states for more than a decade broke that way.
impact: 第一次達契亞戰爭的直接後果，是羅馬第一次把常備的帝國軍推進到多瑙河以北的喀爾巴阡山，並在山區留下成套的堡壘、營壘、掘進坑道與道路；即使隨後在公元118年放棄了多瑙河以東的達契亞行省，這些工事仍然是後來羅馬進入巴爾幹與黑海地區的基礎。從帝國財政看，這場戰爭帶回的達契亞黃金與白銀，讓圖拉真得以在羅馬興建圖拉真廣場與圖拉真柱，柱上銘文明說要用以宣告開闢如此高山與如此工地所耗的巨力，公元102年的凱旋與隨後的紀念工程把一次邊境戰爭轉成首都的建築，也讓「達契亞」變成皇帝頭銜上的一個恆久詞。軍事的教訓同樣具體：這是一場以工程、投射火力、封鎖線與冬季補給取勝的戰爭，後來圖拉真對帕提亞的遠征幾乎照搬同一套做法，先修路、再築橋，推進與補給同步。更長遠的影響落在達契亞人自己身上：山區堡壘被毀、王都被奪、大量戰俘被遷往羅馬與各行省，作為一個獨立的軍事與祭祀共同體的達契亞就此消失，羅馬行省的礦山與金銀稅源把多瑙河南岸的防線長期維繫下去。考古與史學層面，二十世紀初的考古工作確認了奧爾什蒂耶山區的堡壘群即達契亞王都所在，這一認定構成了此後達契亞史研究的基礎，也讓這段遠古戰爭重新進入近代的民族敘事。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the First Dacian War was that Rome carried a permanent imperial army north of the Danube into the Carpathians for the first time, and left behind a whole complex of forts, camps, mining galleries and roads in the mountains; even after the province beyond the Danube was abandoned in AD 118, those works remained the foundation for Rome's later advance into the Balkans and towards the Black Sea. In fiscal terms, the gold and silver brought back from Dacia allowed Trajan to build the Forum of Trajan and Trajan's Column in Rome, and the inscription on the column states plainly that it was set up to declare the great height of the mountain and the great labour of the works; the triumph of AD 102 and the commemorative building that followed turned a frontier war into capital architecture, and made 'Dacian' a permanent word in the emperor's titles. The military lesson was equally concrete: this was a war won by engineering, missile fire, lines of communication and winter supply, and Trajan's later campaign against the Parthians reproduced almost exactly the same method, building roads, then bridges, and keeping the advance and its supply moving together. The longer-term effect fell on the Dacians themselves. The mountain forts were destroyed, the capital was taken, large numbers of prisoners were moved to Rome and the provinces, and the Dacians ceased to exist as an independent military and religious community; the mines and the gold and silver revenues of the new Roman province kept the defence on the southern bank of the Danube in being for a long time. In archaeology and historiography, the early twentieth-century identification of the Orăștie valley forts as the seat of the Dacian kings became the basis of all later work on Dacian history, and it returned this ancient war to modern national narrative.
result: 打完了。公元101年，圖拉真的大軍在圖帕埃打開缺口，奪下達契亞的營帳與大批裝備；公元102年，羅馬軍攻入山區的薩爾米澤蓋圖薩，奪取國王存放於山嶺聖域的財寶，德塞巴魯斯在走投無路中自盡，達契亞王國一時失去國王與寶藏。羅馬隨後因季節與糧秣撤出，多瑙河以北的局勢並未立刻穩定：達契亞貴族另推德塞巴魯斯的親族多米提安（Domitianus）為王，與圖拉真往來談判，達契亞保留了政權的殘餘，羅馬也沒有立刻兼併全境。公元105年至106年的第二次達契亞戰爭才真正打下薩爾米澤蓋圖薩，公元119年左右圖拉真指定的繼承者哈德良把帝國防線退回多瑙河，把達契亞王國改為行省，最終在公元271年至272年由奧勒良放棄。至於第一次戰役的實際規模，學界至今仍有兩種讀法：古典傳統以狄奧為本，認為圖拉真在公元102年攻下王都、奪取國寶；近年的研究則以「科努拉努斯假說」為代表，認為第一次戰役的主要任務是解救了北方被圍的盟友科努拉努斯，王都未必在當時被攻破，兩說相差的正是這座山。兩說並存，反映的正是這場戰爭史料的模樣：唯一成篇的敘述來自一位事後的元老，而留下的物證則分散在山裡。
resultEn: The war was fought and finished. In AD 101 Trajan's army opened a gap at Tapae and took the Dacian camp with much of its equipment; in AD 102 the Romans entered the mountains, seized Sarmizegetusa, and carried off the treasure the king had stored in the sacred precinct of the high place, and Decebalus took his own life when there was nothing left to try, so that the Dacian kingdom was for a time without a king and without its treasure. The Romans then withdrew because of the season and the shortage of supply, and the situation north of the Danube did not settle at once: the Dacian nobility raised another kinsman of Decebalus, Domitianus, to the kingship and negotiated with Trajan, the Dacians kept the remnant of their polity, and Rome did not annex the whole country immediately. It took the second Dacian War of AD 105 to 106 to take Sarmizegetusa for good; around AD 119 Trajan's designated successor Hadrian withdrew the imperial line back to the Danube and turned the Dacian kingdom into a province, and it was finally abandoned under Aurelian in AD 271 to 272. On the actual scale of the first campaign, two readings remain in competition. The classical tradition, following Dio, holds that Trajan took the capital and the treasure in AD 102. More recent work, represented by the 'Cornulannus hypothesis', argues that the main business of the first war was to relieve an ally, Cornulannus, who was besieged in the north, and that the capital may not have been stormed at that time at all; the two readings differ by precisely that mountain. That both readings stand is a fair summary of the state of this evidence: the only continuous narrative comes from a senator writing after the event, and the physical traces lie scattered in the hills.
